```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages(library(ggplot2))
P  <- "/project/xinhe/xsun/GLI-Hedgehog_Signaling"
r  <- read.delim(file.path(P, "results/1.geneset_enrichment/enrichment_fisher.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
gs <- read.delim(file.path(P, "data/gene_sets/enrichment_gene_sets.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
bg <- read.delim(file.path(P, "data/gene_sets/background_protein_coding_hgnc.tsv"))
cl <- read.delim(file.path(P, "data/gene_clusters/maSigPro_clusters_hgnc.tsv"))
sf <- read.delim(file.path(P, "data/gene_sets/SFARI_cat1_cat2_07-12-2026release.tsv"))
nd <- read.delim(file.path(P, "data/gene_sets/NDD_genes.tsv"))

# the two gene sets used on this page
sets <- c(ASD = "SFARI_cat1", NDD = "NDD_wang2022")
lab  <- c(ASD = "ASD (SFARI category 1)", NDD = "NDD (Wang et al. 2022)")
d <- r[r$cluster != "all" & r$gene_set %in% sets, ]
d$set <- names(sets)[match(d$gene_set, sets)]
d$k <- as.integer(d$cluster)
d <- d[order(d$set, d$k), ]
sig <- d[d$p_value < 0.05, ]

f2  <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
pv  <- function(p) ifelse(p >= 0.001, sprintf("%.3f", p), formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 1))
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
get1 <- function(s, k, v) d[d$set == s & d$k == k, v]
# one-line description of a result: "44 genes vs 19.2 expected (2.3x, p = 2.2e-07)"
desc <- function(s, k) paste0(get1(s, k, "overlap"), ifelse(get1(s, k, "overlap") == 1, " gene", " genes"),
                              " vs ", f2(get1(s, k, "expected")),
                              " expected (", f2(get1(s, k, "fold")), "x, p = ", pv(get1(s, k, "p_value")), ")")
ids  <- function(s) gs$hgnc_id[gs$gene_set == sets[[s]]]
n_set <- function(s) length(ids(s))
shared <- length(intersect(ids("ASD"), ids("NDD")))
w <- nd[nd$source == "Wang2022", ]
n_clust <- function(k) sum(cl$kept & cl$cluster == k)

# chart ink and diverging colours (blue = depleted, gray = as expected, red = enriched)
INK <- "#0b0b0b"; INK2 <- "#52514e"; MUTED <- "#898781"
SURF <- "#fcfcfb"; BLUE <- "#2a78d6"; RED <- "#e34948"; MID <- "#f0efec"
```

# Summary

* **Clusters 2 and 6 are enriched for both ASD and NDD genes**, about two-fold
  over what the cluster size predicts.
  * Cluster 2: ASD `r desc("ASD", 2)`; NDD `r desc("NDD", 2)`.
  * Cluster 6: ASD `r desc("ASD", 6)`; NDD `r desc("NDD", 6)`.
* The genes differ between the two clusters. **Cluster 6** genes are largely
  synaptic and neuronal (ion channels, glutamate and GABA receptors, synapse
  proteins), while **cluster 2** genes are mostly chromatin and transcription
  regulators.
* **Cluster 10** is enriched for ASD genes only, more weakly:
  `r desc("ASD", 10)`.
* No other cluster reaches p < 0.05 for either gene set, and no cluster is
  significantly depleted.

# Data

## GLI-response clusters

GLI transcription factors mediate Hedgehog signaling, which shapes how neuronal
progenitors differentiate. In this experiment, GLI is overexpressed and then
perturbed or removed, and gene expression is measured over a time course. Genes
that respond were grouped into **10 clusters** by their expression pattern over
time (maSigPro).

All gene names were updated to current HGNC symbols, using previous symbols and
aliases for outdated names. Only protein-coding genes are kept, to match the
background; most dropped genes are lncRNAs, antisense transcripts or
pseudogenes.

```{r clusters}
k <- sort(unique(cl$cluster))
tab <- data.frame(cluster = k, genes_in_file = as.vector(table(cl$cluster)),
                  kept = as.vector(table(factor(cl$cluster[cl$kept], k))))
tab <- rbind(tab, data.frame(cluster = "total", genes_in_file = sum(tab$genes_in_file), kept = sum(tab$kept)))
knitr::kable(tab, col.names = c("Cluster", "Genes in file", "Protein-coding genes used"),
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## Gene sets

| Gene set | Source | Genes used |
|---|---|---|
| **ASD** | [SFARI Gene](https://gene.sfari.org/), category 1, release 07-12-2026 | `r n_set("ASD")` |
| **NDD** | [Wang et al. 2022, *PNAS*](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2203491119), all 615 candidate genes | `r n_set("NDD")` |

**ASD: SFARI Gene category 1.** SFARI Gene is an expert-curated database of
autism genes, scored by strength of evidence. Category 1 ("high confidence")
genes have been clearly implicated in autism, typically by at least three
de novo likely gene-disrupting mutations reported in the literature. The
07-12-2026 release has `r sum(sf$gene_score == 1)` category 1 genes
(`r sum(sf$gene_score == 1 & sf$syndromic == 1)` also flagged as syndromic);
`r n_set("ASD")` are protein-coding and used here. The three dropped genes are
small nuclear RNA genes (RNU2-2, RNU4-2, RNU5B-1).

**NDD: Wang et al. 2022.** *Integrated gene analyses of de novo variants from
46,612 trios with autism and developmental disorders* (PNAS 119:e2203491119).

* **Data:** exome and genome sequencing of 46,612 parent–child trios from
  11 cohorts: 15,560 with autism (including 6,557 from SPARK) and 31,052
  with developmental delay. Only *de novo* variants are used: variants present
  in the child but in neither parent.
* **Method:** for each gene, the observed number of damaging de novo variants
  (likely gene-disrupting, missense, and severe missense with CADD > 30) is
  compared with the number expected from the gene's mutation rate. Three
  statistical models are used: chimpanzee–human divergence, denovolyzeR and
  DeNovoWEST.
* **Genes:** 615 genes reach FDR < 5% in at least one model. Of these,
  `r sum(w$tier %in% c("high", "med"))` reach FDR < 5% in all three models,
  and `r sum(w$tier == "high")` are exome-wide significant in all three. We use
  all 615 (`r n_set("NDD")` protein-coding).
* Two-thirds of the trios have developmental delay, so the list leans toward
  developmental-delay genes; the paper found no autism-specific genes. It
  updates the earlier Coe et al. 2019 analysis (10,927 cases, 253 genes).

**Overlap.** The two sets share `r shared` genes:
`r n_set("ASD") - shared` genes are ASD-only and `r n_set("NDD") - shared` are
NDD-only. Results for the two sets are therefore related, not independent.

## Test

For each cluster and gene set, a **two-sided Fisher's exact test** compares the
cluster with the rest of the background:

|                    | in gene set | not in gene set |
|--------------------|:-----------:|:---------------:|
| in cluster k       | a | b |
| rest of background | c | d |

* **Background:** the whole genome, i.e. all `r fmt(nrow(bg))` HGNC
  protein-coding genes.
* **Fold enrichment** = observed overlap (a) &divide; the overlap expected from
  the cluster and gene-set sizes alone.
* **p-values** are nominal and not corrected for the `r nrow(d)` tests
  (10 clusters &times; 2 gene sets). About `r round(0.05 * nrow(d), 1)` test
  would reach p < 0.05 by chance.
* The test is two-sided, so it detects depletion (fewer genes than expected)
  as well as enrichment.

# Results

**Left:** fold enrichment (observed / expected). **Right:** −log10 p, signed
by direction. Red = enriched, blue = depleted. Numbers are shown where
p < 0.05; on the left, cells with p &ge; 0.05 are faded.

```{r heatmaps, fig.width=4.2, fig.height=5.2, fig.show="hold", out.width="49%", fig.align="default"}
h <- d
h$set_lab <- factor(ifelse(h$set == "ASD", "ASD\n(SFARI cat 1)", "NDD\n(Wang 2022)"),
                    c("ASD\n(SFARI cat 1)", "NDD\n(Wang 2022)"))
h$cluster_f <- factor(h$k, 10:1)                                  # cluster 1 on top
h$sigp <- h$p_value < 0.05
h$l2  <- pmax(pmin(log2(h$fold), 2), -2)                         # fold, log2, capped at 0.25-4
h$slp <- sign(log(h$odds_ratio + 1e-12)) * -log10(h$p_value)     # signed -log10 p
h$slp_c <- pmax(pmin(h$slp, 10), -10)

th <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), plot.background = element_rect(fill = SURF, colour = NA),
        plot.title = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold", size = 11),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = INK2), axis.text.x = element_text(colour = INK, size = 10),
        axis.title = element_text(colour = INK2),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(colour = INK2, size = 9),
        legend.text = element_text(colour = INK2, size = 9),
        legend.key.width = unit(32, "pt"), legend.key.height = unit(8, "pt"))
bar <- guides(fill = guide_colourbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))
tile <- function(fill_var, lab_txt, white_if, alpha_var = NULL) {
  list(geom_tile(aes(fill = .data[[fill_var]], alpha = if (is.null(alpha_var)) 1 else .data[[alpha_var]]),
                 colour = SURF, linewidth = 1.2),
       scale_alpha_identity(),
       geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(sigp, lab_txt, ""),
                     colour = ifelse(white_if, "#ffffff", INK)), size = 3.6, fontface = "bold"),
       scale_colour_identity())
}

h$a_fold <- ifelse(h$sigp, 1, 0.35)
ggplot(h, aes(set_lab, cluster_f)) +
  tile("l2", f2(h$fold), abs(h$l2) > 1.1, "a_fold") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = BLUE, mid = MID, high = RED, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-2, 2),
                       breaks = log2(c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4)), labels = c("<=0.25", "0.5", "1", "2", ">=4"),
                       name = "Fold") +
  labs(title = "Fold enrichment", x = NULL, y = "Cluster") + th + bar

ggplot(h, aes(set_lab, cluster_f)) +
  tile("slp_c", f2(-log10(h$p_value)), abs(h$slp_c) > 5.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = BLUE, mid = MID, high = RED, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-10, 10),
                       breaks = c(-10, -5, 0, 5, 10), labels = c("<=-10", "-5", "0", "5", ">=10"),
                       name = "Signed -log10 p") +
  labs(title = "-log10 p", x = NULL, y = "Cluster") + th + bar
```

```{r table}
a <- d[d$set == "ASD", ]; n <- d[d$set == "NDD", ]
bold <- function(x, p) ifelse(p < 0.05, paste0("**", x, "**"), x)
tab <- data.frame(
  cluster = a$k, genes = fmt(a$n_cluster),
  a_obs = paste0(a$overlap, " / ", f2(a$expected)), a_fold = bold(sprintf("%.2f", a$fold), a$p_value),
  a_p = bold(pv(a$p_value), a$p_value),
  n_obs = paste0(n$overlap, " / ", f2(n$expected)), n_fold = bold(sprintf("%.2f", n$fold), n$p_value),
  n_p = bold(pv(n$p_value), n$p_value))
knitr::kable(tab, format = "pipe", align = "rrrrrrrr",
             col.names = c("Cluster", "Genes", "ASD: observed / expected", "ASD: fold", "ASD: p",
                           "NDD: observed / expected", "NDD: fold", "NDD: p"),
             caption = "Bold: p < 0.05.")
```

## Cluster by cluster

**Cluster 6** (`r fmt(n_clust(6))` genes, the largest cluster)

* ASD: `r desc("ASD", 6)`. NDD: `r desc("NDD", 6)`.
* The ASD genes are largely **synaptic and neuronal**:
  * ion channels and neurotransmitter receptors: GRIN2B, GRIA2, GABRB3, KCNB1,
    KCNQ2, KCNQ3
  * synapse proteins: DLG4, NRXN1, NRXN2, SHANK2, STXBP1, SYN1, RIMS1
  * neuronal transcription factors: MYT1L, BCL11A, SATB1, TSHZ3, EBF3, ZBTB20
* The NDD genes follow the same pattern, adding synaptic-vesicle and
  channel genes such as SYT1, VAMP2, STX1B, SCN3A, ATP1A3 and KIF1A.

**Cluster 2** (`r fmt(n_clust(2))` genes)

* ASD: `r desc("ASD", 2)`. NDD: `r desc("NDD", 2)`. This is the strongest
  NDD result.
* The genes are mostly **chromatin and transcription regulators**:
  * ASD: ARID1B, ADNP, ATRX, CHD7, CREBBP, EP300, KMT2A, NIPBL, SMARCA4, SETD2,
    SIN3A
  * NDD adds ARID1A, ARID2, CHD4, EZH2, NSD2, SMARCD1 and SMARCE1.
* The NDD genes in this cluster include GLI3 itself.

**Cluster 10** (`r fmt(n_clust(10))` genes)

* ASD: `r desc("ASD", 10)`, including CTNNB1, DDX3X, CHD3 and PCDH19.
* NDD is not enriched: `r desc("NDD", 10)`.

**Other clusters**

* No result reaches p < 0.05.
* A few have fewer ASD genes than expected, but none significantly:
  * cluster 5: `r desc("ASD", 5)`
  * cluster 7: `r desc("ASD", 7)`

The gene-type patterns above come from reading the gene lists; they are
descriptive, not a formal test.

## Genes behind the significant results

```{r genes}
g <- sig[order(sig$k, sig$set), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(g$k, lab[g$set], g$overlap, gsub(",", ", ", g$overlap_genes)),
             col.names = c("Cluster", "Gene set", "Genes", "Overlapping genes"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Notes

* **Strength of evidence.** The four results for clusters 2 and 6 have
  p &le; `r pv(max(d$p_value[d$k %in% c(2, 6)]))`, far below
  0.05 / `r nrow(d)` = `r 0.05 / nrow(d)`. The cluster 10 result
  (p = `r pv(get1("ASD", 10, "p_value"))`) is weaker and could be a chance
  finding.
* **Background.** The genome-wide background includes genes not expressed in
  these cells. Genes expressed in neural progenitors are generally enriched
  for neurodevelopmental genes, which can inflate genome-wide enrichment.
* **Cluster size.** Cluster 6 is the largest cluster, so it has the most power
  to detect enrichment.
* **Mutation-intolerant genes.** Many ASD and NDD genes are highly intolerant
  of damaging mutations. A cluster rich in such genes could look enriched for
  that reason alone; this has not yet been tested.

Detailed results for all 7 gene sets (SFARI categories 1 and 2, TADA tiers,
NDD) are on the [detailed page](geneset_enrichment.html).
